author: (Pallas, 1770)

note.en: The world's largest tern, with a heavy red bill; a rare winter or passage visitor here, seen with royal terns at river mouths and on beaches, with only a few records.
note.es: El charrán más grande del mundo, con un pico rojo pesado; visitante raro de invierno o de paso aquí, visto con charranes reales en desembocaduras y playas, con pocos registros.

evidence: iNaturalist: 5 research-grade records in the region

sources.t: iNaturalist taxon page and regional observations
Garrigues & Dean, The Birds of Costa Rica: A Field Guide (2nd ed., 2014), status and range

recWhy: Five iNaturalist records in the region; sites not stated.

marks.en: Largest tern, with a heavy red-orange bill and a black cap.
marks.es: La gaviota más grande, con un pico pesado rojo anaranjado y casquete negro.
